title: Hastings Street and the Ace Bar
summary: Hastings Street's games, bars and pimps, his first job there with George E. Lee, and Milt Jackson jamming around.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And then the other main vein, where the action was, where all the prostitutes and pimps hung out, was Hastings Street. All the way up and down Hastings, there was guys in the daytime, they'd be running their three card molly, and
(?)ing the greasy pig with the shells and the pea, and all kinds of games would be going on. And they had bars all up and down that street.

My first job up on Hastings Street was at a place called the Ace Bar, and I was working with the legendary band-leader from George E. Lee. And he was an elderly man, and he was singing and using a megaphone, you know -- that was quite an experience.

And I used to go all up and down the street to different places and play. They had a place called the Cozy Corner, where Bill... Wild Bill Moore had the band up there. And Milt Jackson was just beginning to get himself together during that period, and he used to be running all over town to different places, jamming. His brother would pack one end of the vibes and he'd have the other end -- and his brother also played bass. And they would be all the place, playing the different scenes.
